section_summary: The section ends a glossary of Japanese fisheries terms, then turns to 1947 correspondence about Japanese fishing policy and Antarctic whaling. State Department, SCAP, and other officials debate fishing limits, whaling authorization, fleet routes, catch reporting, and statistical requests. An enclosed report reviews Japan’s prewar whaling industry and its economic prospects.

people.name: Edward W. Allen
people.role: International fisheries commissioner and Seattle attorney consulted on fishing policy

people.name: W. E. S. Flory
people.role: Acting Assistant Chief, International Resources Division

people.name: Mr. Phister

people.name: H. S. Deason
people.role: Chief, Office of Foreign Activities, Fish and Wildlife Service

people.role: Fish and Wildlife Service biologist compiling Japanese whaling statistics

people.role: Director of the International Bureau for Whaling Statistics

people.name: John Allison
people.role: State Department official who requested the whaling industry report

people.name: Hugh Borton
people.role: Recipient of a State Department memorandum

subfiles.title: Glossary of Japanese Fisheries Terms, concluding pages
subfiles.about: Alphabetical English and Japanese fisheries vocabulary from oyster drill through Zuwai crab.
subfiles.summary: The closing pages of Natural Resources Section Report 63 provide English and romanized Japanese names for fish, shellfish, seaweed, marine mammals, fishing gear, facilities, and fishery practices. Many entries include scientific names, alternative terms, or cross references.

subfiles.title: List of Natural Resources Section Reports
subfiles.about: Lists Natural Resources Section reports numbered 1 through 63.
subfiles.summary: Lists report titles and dates, including fisheries and whaling related studies.

subfiles.title: Distribution of Report 63
subfiles.about: Specifies recipients and copy counts for the fisheries glossary.
subfiles.summary: Distribution list for military, diplomatic, and Natural Resources Section offices.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram on Australian fishing policy proposal
subfiles.about: Requests SCAP consultation before a United States position or FEC decision on Japanese fishing is fixed.
subfiles.summary: Tokyo stresses Japanese fishing’s importance to food supply and asks that SCAP review policy developments.

subfiles.title: Whale catch report for December 16–22
subfiles.about: Transmits 26 blue whale units caught by the Japanese expedition for forwarding to Sandefjord.
subfiles.summary: Asks the embassy to forward the first weekly catch figure pending clarification of direct SCAP reporting.

subfiles.title: Instructions to SCAP on whale catch reporting
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Seeks factory ship catch breakdowns and confirmation of notification to the United Kingdom.
subfiles.summary: Cites the 1945 whaling protocol and requests direct weekly reports for each factory ship.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Mr. Allen on Japanese fishing policy
subfiles.about: Discusses whether a 50-mile protective boundary would protect American fishing interests.
subfiles.summary: Allen notes a halibut ground roughly 100 miles off Kodiak Island but doubts Japanese exploitation would be practical. He considers the proposed boundary reasonable protection.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Mr. Phister on Japanese fishing policy
subfiles.about: Seeks Phister’s response to a proposed 50-mile restriction.
subfiles.summary: Phister notes tuna grounds off Ecuador but considers near-term Japanese exploitation economically unlikely.

subfiles.title: Whale catch report for December 23–29
subfiles.about: Forwards a weekly catch of 73 blue whale units to Sandefjord.
subfiles.summary: Requests onward transmission while awaiting SCAP’s answer on direct reporting.

subfiles.title: United States draft policy for Japanese fishing
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Reports the American counterproposal to Australian restrictions on Japanese marine industries.
subfiles.summary: The draft encourages Japanese fishing, whaling, pearl fishing, and related industries while proposing a 50-mile exclusion around foreign land areas, specified exceptions, passage rules, and conservation requirements. It reports disagreement at the FEC subcommittee and seeks SCAP comments before its next meeting.

subfiles.title: Japanese fisheries book sent for translation review
subfiles.about: Asks for assessment and possible acquisition of a Japanese fisheries book.
subfiles.summary: Deason forwards photostats and asks the Central Translating Division to determine the book’s contents.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Japanese fisheries book
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of the book photostats and their referral for translation.
subfiles.summary: Promises to send Deason the completed translation.

subfiles.title: Record-copy replacement notice
subfiles.about: Designates a telegram or airgram copy as the record copy.
subfiles.summary: The white copy replaces an unreturned yellow action copy.

subfiles.title: SCAP reply on catch reporting and British notification
subfiles.about: Explains reporting difficulties and supplies factory ship catch breakdowns.
subfiles.summary: SCAP says it lacks a direct circuit to Norway, gives catches for Hashidate Maru and Nisshin Maru, and reports formal notification to the British mission.

subfiles.title: Proposed urgent cable on direct reporting
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Suggests a commercial cable route for timely factory ship catch reports.
subfiles.summary: State proposes transmission via San Francisco, New York, and Oslo to meet the protocol’s two-day deadline.

subfiles.title: Revised urgent cable on direct reporting
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Presses SCAP to report each ship’s weekly catch within the treaty deadline.
subfiles.summary: Proposes commercial communications and asks for reasons if timely reporting is impossible.

subfiles.title: Corrected telegram on return route of Japanese whaling fleet
subfiles.about: Provides the planned return route from Antarctica to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The corrected copy traces the route past Bougainville and the Green Islands and notes a possible reversal of the outward route.

subfiles.title: Telegram on return route of Japanese whaling fleet
subfiles.about: Requests formal notice to interested governments of the whaling fleet’s return route.
subfiles.summary: The original copy gives the route and reserves a possible reversal due to unforeseen circumstances; it is marked superseded by a corrected copy.

subfiles.title: SCAP comments on proposed FEC fisheries policy
subfiles.about: Urges opposition to Australian proposed restrictions on Japanese fishing and whaling.
subfiles.summary: SCAP argues that existing directives protect Allied interests while allowing prompt administration and food production. It warns that the proposal could delay fishing decisions and prevent factory ship whaling near the Bonin Islands. It describes the current Antarctic expedition as a one-season emergency measure.

subfiles.title: Reply to Edward W. Allen on public consultation
subfiles.about: Explains how the Department consults the public on international fisheries policy.
subfiles.summary: Flory favors public discussion where feasible but explains limits when several governments share responsibility and confidential talks are underway.

subfiles.title: Factory ship breakdown sent to Oslo
subfiles.about: Forwards revised factory ship figures for three weeks of Japanese Antarctic catches.
subfiles.summary: Asks the embassy to inform Sandefjord while efforts continue to establish direct reporting.

subfiles.title: Oslo report on Sandefjord’s reporting requirements
subfiles.about: Reports the Bureau’s request for direct, timely catch reports.
subfiles.summary: Sandefjord received earlier figures but says inspectors must report directly to meet the treaty deadline.

subfiles.title: SCAP establishes direct weekly catch reporting
subfiles.about: Reports direct transmission to Sandefjord and revises season-to-date catch figures.
subfiles.summary: SCAP says reports now travel by Japanese wireless through Geneva and supplies revised figures through January 18.

subfiles.title: Cover memorandum for The Japanese Whaling Industry
subfiles.about: Forwards an information note on Japan’s whaling industry.
subfiles.summary: Sends a report prepared in response to John Allison’s request.

subfiles.title: The Japanese Whaling Industry
subfiles.about: Analyzes prewar Japanese coastal, colonial, and Antarctic whaling and future economic prospects.
subfiles.summary: The report traces increased catches and value in Japanese waters during the 1930s, alongside declining colonial catches. It describes rapid expansion of Antarctic fleets and whale oil production, noting the importance of oil and export earnings. Tables compare catches, fleet size, crews, and product values. Future Antarctic operations are presented as economically significant and dependent on Allied policy.

subfiles.title: Authorization of Japanese Whaling in Antarctic
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Encloses formal notification of British authorities about the Japanese expedition.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the January 15 SCAP note and January 23 British acknowledgment.

subfiles.title: Formal notification of Japanese Antarctic whaling
subfiles.to: United Kingdom Liaison Mission in Japan
subfiles.about: Formally notifies Britain of authorization for the 1946–47 Japanese Antarctic expedition.
subfiles.summary: Quotes the authorized whaling area and requests transmission to His Majesty’s Government.

subfiles.title: British acknowledgment of whaling notification
subfiles.from: United Kingdom Liaison Mission in Japan
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt and forwarding of the Japanese expedition notice.
subfiles.summary: Confirms that the notice was sent to the British foreign secretary.

subfiles.title: Letter to Allen on proposed fisheries directive
subfiles.about: Thanks Allen for his views and encloses the current directive and a draft revision.
subfiles.summary: Says FEC has reached no decision and invites further suggestions.

subfiles.title: Internal note on consultation with Allen and Phister
subfiles.about: Explains the established consultation relationship with two fisheries advisers.
subfiles.summary: Describes Allen’s commissions and Phister’s California fisheries committee.

subfiles.title: Letter to Phister on proposed fisheries directive
subfiles.about: Thanks Phister for his comments and sends fisheries policy materials.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the current directive and draft revision and invites further views.

subfiles.title: Return route notice to British Embassy
subfiles.about: Notifies Britain of the Japanese whaling fleet’s planned return route.
subfiles.summary: Describes the route through the southwest Pacific and notes a remote possibility of reversing the outward route through Lombok Strait.

subfiles.title: Return route notice to New Zealand Legation
subfiles.about: Notifies New Zealand of the Japanese whaling fleet’s planned return route.
subfiles.summary: Gives the southwest Pacific route and reserves a possible reversal of the outward passage.

subfiles.title: Whale catch report for January 19–25
subfiles.about: Reports each factory ship’s weekly blue whale unit catch.
subfiles.summary: Reports 20 units for Hashidate Maru and 50½ for Nisshin Maru, with direct reporting to Sandefjord.

subfiles.title: Fish and Wildlife Service letter on delayed statistical analysis
subfiles.about: Explains why Japanese whaling statistics cannot meet Sandefjord’s spring publication deadline.
subfiles.summary: Gilmore’s naval Antarctic assignment delays the analysis; a report is expected around September.

subfiles.title: Request for Japanese whaling statistics
subfiles.about: Requests detailed Japanese statistics for the next International Whaling Statistics issue.
subfiles.summary: Asks when Gilmore’s analysis and 1946 coastal catch figures can be supplied.

subfiles.title: Instructions to Oslo on delayed whaling analysis
subfiles.about: Asks the embassy to inform Paulsen of the delay in Japanese statistical analysis.
subfiles.summary: Explains Gilmore’s assignment and gives September as the expected completion date.

subfiles.title: Oslo request for Japanese expedition details
subfiles.about: Seeks vessel specifications and crew data for two Japanese whaling expeditions.
subfiles.summary: Paulsen requests catcher names, tonnage, horsepower, and crew numbers and nationalities.

subfiles.title: Instructions on Japanese whaling vessel flags
subfiles.about: Reports instructions on flags flown by Japanese whaling vessels.
subfiles.summary: American representatives were told to fly only the modified International Letter E flag.

subfiles.title: Whale catch report for January 26–February 1
subfiles.about: Reports weekly blue whale unit catches by factory ship.
subfiles.summary: Reports 31 units for Hashidate Maru and 48 for Nisshin Maru.

subfiles.title: Notice to Oslo on direct whaling reports
subfiles.about: Advises that SCAP now sends weekly catch reports directly to Sandefjord.
subfiles.summary: Asks the embassy to report if Sandefjord does not receive them.
